title: Command

act2.summary: undo/redo, then a macro command made of commands, including a macro nested inside a macro

solutions.title: Action records turned into Command objects that know how to undo themselves
solutions.tradeoff: Every action becomes an object with an execute() and an undo() instead of a case in a switch. The price: two files and a factory function sit between an ActionRecord and the effect it has, for two action kinds that could have stayed a six-line switch forever if undo had never been asked for.

reviewFocus: Does MacroCommand's undo() reverse sub-commands in the correct (reverse) order, and does a macro nested inside a macro still undo as one unit?
Is RotateWheelCommand capturing fromSlot at construction time or at execute() time - and does the walkthrough explain why that choice matters for a command sitting in a macro before it runs?
Is there still exactly one place (the factory) that knows which ActionRecord becomes which Command, or did that knowledge leak into the panel or the queue?
Is the walkthrough honest that the no-pattern baseline wins on file count and hunk count, and that lines-touched is the axis that actually tells this story?
Would a plain function-based Command (a record of two closures, execute and undo, instead of a class implementing an interface) have been a reasonable alternative here?
